minor.issue: 5-failed-attempt lockout is scoped to request.client.host:email but preview ingress can serve consecutive requests from different upstream IPs, so 429 isn't reliably reached from an external caller. The DB accumulates multiple login_attempts docs (one per IP), each with count<5. Consider keying the identifier on X-Forwarded-For head or on email alone (with a longer window) so brute-force protection works behind the ingress. In tests we forced a doc to count=5 to prove the read path.

ui_bugs.issue: Field-name mismatch with backend contract: component reads h.ratings?.a and h.ratings?.b, but backend coparenting_tiers._ratings() returns keys parent_a / parent_b (matches ScoreTrendChart.jsx which correctly uses ratings?.parent_a / ratings?.parent_b). Result: rows [data-testid=compare-row-a] and [data-testid=compare-row-b] render '—' for both v1 and v2 and their [data-testid=compare-delta-a] / -delta-b show '—' regardless of any rating change. Fix: change (h) => h.ratings?.a to (h) => h.ratings?.parent_a and (h) => h.ratings?.b to (h) => h.ratings?.parent_b in the metrics array. Verified via backend test test_reassessment_compare_shape_matches_frontend.

action_items: Fix ReassessmentCompare.jsx metrics rows to read h.ratings?.parent_a and h.ratings?.parent_b (currently h.ratings?.a / .b) so the Parent A/B rating and delta cells populate for compare-row-a, compare-row-b, compare-delta-a, compare-delta-b. ScoreTrendChart already uses the correct keys — align the two.
Optional: strengthen brute-force lockout so it works behind the preview/prod ingress (identifier not tied to request.client.host, e.g., email-only or X-Forwarded-For).
critical_code_review_comments: coparenting_tiers._ratings returns {parent_a, parent_b, joint} — that is the source of truth used by pdf_report and ScoreTrendChart. ReassessmentCompare invented its own {a,b,joint} shape that never matches. Enforce a shared TS/JSDoc type or write a shape test in the FE.

auth.forgot_password inserts a password_resets doc AFTER deleting older ones for the same email but BEFORE send_email; on send failure it deletes them again — this leaves the caller with a 60s throttle that can silently mask send outages. Consider inserting only after send succeeds, or don't count send-failure requests toward the 60s window.

auth.login lockout uses request.client.host:email as identifier — behind a proxy the host is the ingress IP (or one of several), so a rotating pool defeats the 5-attempt lockout entirely. Combine with request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For') or key by email + user-agent hash.

auth.reset_password: when token is provided but new_password<8, it 400s BEFORE the token lookup — good, but the message 'Password must be at least 8 characters' still leaks that a valid token was not required to get that error. Not a real enumeration issue but consider order-of-checks consistency.

ReassessmentCompare imports lucide-react and text-align-green class; verify the tailwind color token exists (align-green is in the palette; text-align-green class must be enabled in tailwind.config.js safelist for JIT — otherwise the green +delta won't get its color).

Frontend fix to verify after main agent patches: /court/case/{ref_id} as an approved judge with 2 submissions — assert [data-testid=compare-row-a] second and third cells show numeric ratings (not '—') and [data-testid=compare-delta-a] shows a signed integer badge (arrow-up/down icon + '+N' or '-N'). The bug is a pure JSX field-name swap (a→parent_a, b→parent_b) in ReassessmentCompare.jsx lines 20-21. Data contract: level_history[i].ratings = {parent_a: int|null, parent_b: int|null, joint: int|null}; .growth = {a:{met,total,items:[{text,met}]}, b:{...}}; .score = statement.framework.score (requires professional-statement dynamic_score set at each submission).
rca of the issue: ReassessmentCompare.jsx (added this iteration) reads h.ratings?.a / h.ratings?.b for the Parent-A/-B rating rows, but the backend contract in /app/backend/coparenting_tiers.py::_ratings() has always used the keys parent_a / parent_b (as consumed by ScoreTrendChart.jsx and pdf_report.py). The component ships next to a chart that reads the correct keys, so the mismatch was likely a copy from an earlier draft. Reproduction: submit-to-court twice on the same case with different parent_a_rating/parent_b_rating; open /court/case/{ref_id} as the judge; compare-row-a / -b previous & current cells render '—' and compare-delta-a / -b render '—'; compare-row-level, compare-row-joint, compare-row-growth-a, compare-row-growth-b populate correctly. Mitigation: one-line replace in /app/frontend/src/components/ReassessmentCompare.jsx of `h.ratings?.a` → `h.ratings?.parent_a` and `h.ratings?.b` → `h.ratings?.parent_b`.
